expected_level_description: You can: - manage service components to ensure they meet business needs and key performance indicators (KPIs)

You can: - explain the importance of developing process efficiency and the common ways in which processes are optimised - support specific activities to improve development processes - identify obvious deficiencies
You can: - design solutions and services with security controls included, specifically engineered to mitigate security threats
You can: - explain the most important principles of modern development standards and how they apply to your work - apply modern development standards principles under guidance

You can: - collaborate with others when necessary to review specifications - use the agreed specifications to design, code, test and document programs or scripts of medium-to-high complexity, using the right standards and tools

You can: - approach prototyping as a team activity, actively soliciting prototypes and testing with others - establish design patterns and iterate them - use a variety of prototyping methods and choose the most appropriate
You can: - identify, locate and fix service faults

You can: - translate logical designs into physical designs - produce detailed designs - effectively document all work using required standards, methods and tools, including prototyping tools where appropriate - design systems characterised by managed levels of risk, manageable business and technical complexity, and meaningful impact - work with well understood technology and identify appropriate patterns
You can: - build and test simple interfaces between systems - work on more complex integration as part of a wider team

You can: - identify and engage with users or stakeholders to collate user needs evidence - understand and define research that fits user needs - use quantitative and qualitative data about users to turn user focus into outcomes

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - run vulnerability scans and report the results - track fixes with system owners
You can: - create, change, and remove user accounts and access rights - check access against role-based access rules
